newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Boral to float off gas business.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Boral to float off gas business.

text.p: Australian industrial group Boral Ltd said on Monday it planned to float off its gas distribution networks in South Australia, Queensland and Northern Territory.
The company said it envisaged sales proceeds of more than A$850 million (US$637.5 million) through the float of a company, to be known as Envestra Ltd.
Boral said it would retain a 19.9 percent stake in the new company and that it expected the transaction to be earnings positive from the outset.

"Energy is a core business and one that Boral intends to grow further by realising the significant opportunities available through deregulation," Boral managing director Tony Berg said in a statement.
"As part of its ongoing strategy, Boral Energy is being restructured to be more focused and efficient and better equipped to take advantage of those opportunities," he said.

"This transaction allows us to realise the value inherent in our natural gas distribution assets, while giving us the flexibility to reinvest the proceeds in new opportunities in the energy industry," Berg said.

Berg said that since Boral's purchase of South Australia's' SAGASCO in 1993, the company had sought to increase its exposure to energy, having identified this industry as one offering a host of opportunities in a deregulated environment.
He said Boral would continue to retail and market gas to its established customer base through its Boral Energy unit as well as boost its upstream production and exploration activities.
Boral said sale proceeds to be received from the sale of gas distribution networks had yet to be finalised, but it was envisaged that net sale proceeds would exceed A$850 million.
It said funds raised would be used to retire debt.
"The board will also seek investment opportunities in Boral's core businesses to enhance shareholder value," it said.
"This transaction will be earnings positive for Boral from the outset," the company said.
